# Postmortem: orders-api outage, 2026-09-29

**Severity:** SEV1 · **Duration:** 4h 02m (13:50–17:52 UTC) · **Status:** resolved, remediations in progress

## Summary

A tax-service release made its quote endpoint about 250× slower without making it fail. orders-api calls that endpoint while holding a Postgres connection inside an open transaction, with a 30 s client timeout. Within minutes every pooled connection was held by a request waiting on tax-service, and all orders-api endpoints failed, including those that never call tax-service. Diagnosis took two hours because the symptoms pointed at the database, and mitigation took another two because the timeout was hard-coded and the downstream rollback was blocked.

## Impact

- About 85% of orders-api requests (checkout, order status, order history) failed or timed out for 4h 02m.
- inventory-api was partially unavailable for 23 minutes (14:35–14:58) as a side effect of our own mitigation attempt.
- No data loss; held transactions rolled back cleanly.

## Timeline (UTC)

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:42 | tax-service deploys a release with a schema migration; `POST /tax/quote` p99 climbs from 90 ms to over 20 s. Its error rate stays flat, so no alert fires. |
| 13:47 | orders-api DB pool utilisation reaches 100% on all 12 pods. |
| 13:50 | **Impact begins.** 5xx rate passes 5%; requests fail with `pool acquisition timeout`. |
| 13:55 | Page fires on orders-api 5xx rate; acknowledged 13:58. |
| 14:05 | SEV1 declared. Working theory: Postgres is degraded. |
| 14:10 | Pods begin restarting: the liveness probe queries the DB and fails when the pool is exhausted. |
| 14:20 | DB team finds Postgres healthy (CPU 15%, no lock contention) but with most connections `idle in transaction`. This is not followed up. |
| 14:35 | orders-api scaled from 12 to 24 pods. Connection demand (480) exceeds headroom under `max_connections` (400); Postgres rejects connections and inventory-api starts failing. |
| 14:50 | Scale-up reverted; inventory-api recovers by 14:58. |
| 15:25 | Postgres primary failover attempted. No improvement. |
| 15:55 | **Cause identified.** Traces show 30 s `POST /tax/quote` spans inside the checkout transaction. |
| 16:05 | tax-service team paged; confirms the regression and starts a rollback. |
| 16:30 | Rollback abandoned: the migration is not reversible. tax-service starts a fix-forward (index build, estimated 60–90 min). |
| 16:40 | Decision to hotfix orders-api in parallel: cut the tax client timeout from 30 s to 2 s. |
| 17:15 | Hotfix built. Canary gate fails against the already-degraded baseline; incident commander approves a manual override. |
| 17:35 | Hotfix fully rolled out. Pool utilisation drops to about 40%; non-checkout endpoints recover. Checkout fails fast. |
| 17:48 | tax-service index build completes; p99 back to 95 ms. |
| 17:52 | **Impact ends.** Error rate below 0.1%. |
| 18:30 | Incident closed after monitoring. |

## Root cause

The checkout handler opens a database transaction, then calls tax-service synchronously, then writes the order. The DB connection is held for the full duration of the remote call. With tax-service at 90 ms this was invisible. At 20–30 s per call and about 35 checkouts per second, demand was roughly 1,000 connections against 240 available (12 pods × pool of 20). The pool saturated in under five minutes.

The trigger was the tax-service regression: a migration dropped an index its quote query relied on. The root cause is ours: orders-api let a slow dependency hold a scarce shared resource with no bound short enough to matter.

## Contributing factors

**Why the blast radius was total**
- One pool served every endpoint, so checkout starved read-only endpoints that have no tax-service dependency.
- The 30 s timeout was a library default, over 300× the normal p99.
- There was no circuit breaker, and web and mobile clients retried failed requests, roughly doubling load.
- The DB-dependent liveness probe restarted pods that were otherwise functional, adding churn.

**Why diagnosis took two hours**
- The only alerting signal was pool exhaustion, which reads as a database problem.
- Neither side alerted on tax-service latency: tax-service alerted on error rate only, and orders-api had no per-dependency latency alerts or dashboard.
- The `idle in transaction` observation at 14:20 was the key clue, and no runbook told anyone what it means.

**Why mitigation took two more hours**
- The timeout was hard-coded, so changing it needed a build and deploy; there was no kill switch for the tax call.
- Scaling up made things worse, because nothing limits pods × pool size against the Postgres connection budget.
- The tax-service migration could not be rolled back.
- The canary gate has no documented break-glass path for deploying into an ongoing incident.

## Remediations

| # | Action | Owner | Due |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fetch the tax quote before opening the transaction; no remote calls while holding a DB connection | Orders | Done (10-02) |
| 2 | Explicit timeouts on every outbound call in orders-api, sized from the dependency's p99 (tax: 2 s total) | Orders | Done (10-02) |
| 3 | Set `idle_in_transaction_session_timeout` to 10 s on the orders database as a backstop | DB | 10-16 |
| 4 | Circuit breaker on the tax client; product to decide fallback (fail fast vs. accept order and reconcile tax later) | Orders, Product | 10-23 |
| 5 | Bulkhead: cap concurrent checkouts or give them a separate pool so reads survive | Orders | 10-30 |
| 6 | Move the DB check from liveness to readiness probe | Orders | 10-16 |
| 7 | Alert on per-dependency p99 latency from orders-api; alert on count and age of `idle in transaction` connections | Orders, DB | 10-16 |
| 8 | tax-service: alert on p99 latency, not only error rate | Tax | 10-16 |
| 9 | Runbook for pool exhaustion: check what the held connections are waiting on first; do not scale up | Orders | 10-16 |
| 10 | Make timeouts runtime-configurable and add a kill switch for the tax call | Orders | 10-30 |
| 11 | Enforce pods × pool size ≤ connection budget in the autoscaler, or put PgBouncer in front | Platform | 11-13 |
| 12 | tax-service: migrations must be reversible, and query plans checked against production-sized data before release | Tax | 11-13 |
| 13 | Document a break-glass path for the canary gate during incidents | Platform | 10-23 |
| 14 | Audit other services for remote calls made inside transactions and for default timeouts | All service owners | 11-27 |

Items 1–3 alone would have prevented this outage; 7 and 9 would have cut diagnosis from two hours to minutes.
